# Purpose

When Bgee compares gene expression **across species**, it must decide which anatomical
structures (and cell types) can be treated as **homologous** — i.e. as valid targets
for a single multi-species comparison group.

Biocurators annotate these decisions in the Bgee **similarity annotation** dataset.
There are two kinds of statement:

| Kind | Meaning | Typical use |
|------|---------|-------------|
| **Positive** | The listed UBERON term(s) designate **one** homologous structure (or one homologous *relation* between structures) for all species in the annotated taxon lineage. | "Lung and swim bladder are homologous in Gnathostomata." |
| **Negative** (`negated = true`) | The listed UBERON term(s) do **not** designate a single homologous structure across the annotated taxon — even though the same ontology label may apply in different lineages. | "Eye is **not** homologous across Bilateria" (vertebrate camera eye vs arthropod compound eye). |

**Homology resolution** is the process of turning these curator annotations into
`AnatEntitySimilarity` objects: the comparison units used by
`MultiSpeciesCallService` (including the
[`multispec_expr_calls` API](multispec_expr_calls_endpoint.qmd)).

This document explains the data model, the resolution algorithm (including negative
annotations), the different outcome paths, and worked examples.

---

# Core concepts

## Anatomical entity vs similarity group

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
flowchart LR
    UBERON["UBERON term<br/>(e.g. UBERON:0002101 limb)"]
    AE["AnatEntity<br/>(Java wrapper, id = UBERON ID)"]
    AES["AnatEntitySimilarity<br/>(comparison unit)"]
    MSC["MultiSpeciesCondition<br/>(used in API output)"]

    UBERON --> AE
    AE --> AES
    AES --> MSC

    style UBERON fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#e65100
    style AES fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
    style MSC fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
```

- An **`AnatEntity`** is a one-to-one wrapper around a UBERON (or CL) identifier.
  The same UBERON ID always maps to the same `AnatEntity` object identity in code
  (`Entity.equals` is based on ID only).
- An **`AnatEntitySimilarity`** is a **comparison unit**: a set of one or more
  `AnatEntity` objects that Bgee will pool for cross-species expression analysis,
  together with supporting annotation metadata.
- We **never** create duplicate `AnatEntity` instances for the same UBERON term with
  different taxa. When a term must be split because of non-homology, we emit **several
  `AnatEntitySimilarity` objects** that share the same `AnatEntity` but are scoped
  to different sub-clades via their annotation summaries.

## Taxon-scoped annotations

Every summary similarity annotation is attached to an NCBI **taxon**. An annotation
at taxon *T* is considered valid for a requested taxon *R* if it is annotated to *R*
or to an **ancestor** of *R* (when loading positives for the baseline), or to *R* or
an ancestor (when loading negatives that block a group at *R*).

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 8
flowchart TB
    subgraph ancestors["Valid blocking negatives for requested taxon R"]
        A1["Annotation at R"]
        A2["Annotation at ancestor of R"]
    end
    R["Requested taxon R<br/>(e.g. Bilateria)"]
    D1["Strict descendant<br/>(e.g. Gnathostomata)"]
    D2["Strict descendant<br/>(e.g. Arthropoda)"]

    A1 --> R
    A2 --> R
    R --> D1
    R --> D2

    style R fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
```

For **sub-clade splitting**, only **strict descendants** of *R* (taxa strictly below
*R* in the taxonomy) can supply replacement positive annotations.

## Single-entity vs multi-entity annotations

Most annotations involve a **single** UBERON term (e.g. `{lung}`).
Some involve **several** terms that are declared homologous **with each other**
(e.g. `{lung, swim bladder}` at Gnathostomata).

Matching between a blocking negative and descendant positives is always on the
**exact set of UBERON IDs**:

| Negative annotation | Matching descendant positive | Does **not** match |
|--------------------|------------------------------|--------------------|
| `{UBERON:0002048 lung}` | `{lung}` at Gnathostomata | `{lung, swim bladder}` |
| `{lung, swim bladder}` | `{lung, swim bladder}` at Gnathostomata | `{lung}` alone |

## Annotation summaries on each similarity

Each `AnatEntitySimilarity` carries one or more
`AnatEntitySimilarityTaxonSummary` records:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `taxon` | Taxon at which the supporting annotation was made |
| `trusted` | Whether the CIO confidence statement is trusted |
| `positive` | `true` = positive homology support; `false` = negative (non-homology) documentation |

After negative-aware resolution, a sub-clade similarity typically carries **positive**
summaries from descendant taxa **plus** the **negative** summary that explains why
the term was split at the requested level.

# Data storage and programming interfaces

## Database layer (summary annotations)

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| `SummarySimilarityAnnotationDAO` | Summary annotations with `negated`, `taxonId`, `CIOId` |
| `SummarySimilarityAnnotationTO.isNegated()` | `true` = negative (NOT homologous) |
| `getSummarySimilarityAnnotations(..., positiveAnnots, ...)` | Filter: `true` = positives only, `false` = negatives only, `null` = both |
| `getSimAnnotToAnatEntity(...)` | Links annotation ID → UBERON entity ID(s) |
| `RawSimilarityAnnotationDAO` | Individual evidence lines (ECO, reference, curator, supporting text) |

## Service layer

| Method | Behaviour | Used by |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `loadPositiveAnatEntitySimilarities(taxonId, onlyTrusted)` | Positive annotations only; applies multi-entity vs single-entity selection logic | Legacy callers, `loadSimilarityExpressionCalls` (v1) |
| `loadAnatEntitySimilaritiesRespectingNegations(taxonId, onlyTrusted)` | Baseline positives **plus** negative-aware blocking and sub-clade splitting | `loadSimilarityExpressionCalls2`, **`multispec_expr_calls` API** |

# Resolution algorithm

Entry point:
`AnatEntitySimilarityService.loadAnatEntitySimilaritiesRespectingNegations`.

## High-level flow

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
flowchart TD
    START(["Input: requested taxon R,<br/>onlyTrusted flag"]) --> BASELINE["① Baseline<br/>loadPositiveAnatEntitySimilarities(R)"]
    BASELINE --> NEG["② Load negative annotations<br/>at R or ancestors<br/>(grouped by UBERON ID set)"]
    NEG --> EMPTY{"Any blocking<br/>negatives?"}
    EMPTY -->|No| FAST["**Fast path**<br/>Return baseline unchanged"]
    EMPTY -->|Yes| DROP["③ Remove from baseline any similarity<br/>whose UBERON ID set is blocked"]
    DROP --> DESC["④ Load positive annotations<br/>at strict descendants of R<br/>(same UBERON ID sets as blocked groups)"]
    DESC --> SUB{"Any descendant<br/>positives for<br/>blocked sets?"}
    SUB -->|No| DROPONLY["**Block-and-drop path**<br/>Return filtered baseline<br/>(blocked terms absent)"]
    SUB -->|Yes| SPLIT["⑤ For each blocked set:<br/>group descendant positives<br/>by *maximal* taxon"]
    SPLIT --> EMIT["⑥ Emit sub-clade<br/>AnatEntitySimilarity objects<br/>(+ attach negative summaries)"]
    EMIT --> MERGE["⑦ Merge: filtered baseline<br/>+ sub-clade similarities"]
    MERGE --> OUT(["Output: Set of AnatEntitySimilarity"])

    style FAST fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style DROPONLY fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#e65100
    style EMIT fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
```

## Step-by-step

### ① Baseline (positive-only logic)

The baseline is exactly what `loadPositiveAnatEntitySimilarities` would return.
That method already implements substantial curation logic:

- Selects **multiple-entity** vs **single-entity** annotations (e.g. keep
  `lung–swim bladder` at Gnathostomata but separate `mouth` and `anus` at Bilateria).
- Adds `transformation_of`-linked developmental terms where appropriate.
- Filters by trusted/untrusted CIO statements when requested.

The baseline represents "what we would compare **if** no negative annotation blocked
a group at *R* or above."

### ② Identify blocked groups

A **blocked group** is a set of UBERON IDs *G* for which there exists at least one
**negative** summary annotation on *G*, annotated to taxon *R* or any **ancestor** of *R*.

### ③ Remove blocked groups from baseline

Any baseline `AnatEntitySimilarity` whose `sourceAnatEntities` ID set equals a
blocked *G* is **discarded**. A negative at *R* (or an ancestor) overrides an
implicit positive inherited from higher in the tree.

### ④–⑥ Sub-clade splitting (slow path)

If blocked groups exist **and** there are **positive** annotations on the **same**
UBERON ID set *G* at **strict descendants** of *R*:

1. Collect all such descendant positive annotations for *G*.
2. Determine **maximal** annotation taxa among them: taxon *M* is maximal if no
   other annotation taxon in the set is an **ancestor** of *M*.
3. For each maximal taxon *M*, emit one `AnatEntitySimilarity`:
   - `sourceAnatEntities` = entities in *G* (same UBERON terms as before),
   - `requestedTaxon` = *R* (the taxon the user queried),
   - `annotTaxonSummaries` = all descendant **positive** summaries in *M*'s subtree,
     **plus** the blocking **negative** summaries (`positive = false`).

**Maximal-taxong grouping** avoids duplicate similarities when annotations nest
(e.g. `lung` positive at Gnathostomata **and** at Sarcopterygii → one merged group),
while still producing **separate** similarities for **disjoint** sub-clades (e.g.
`eye` positive at Vertebrata **and** at Arthropoda → two groups).

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
flowchart TB
    subgraph nested["Nested descendants → ONE similarity"]
        B1["Negative: lung @ Bilateria"]
        P1["Positive: lung @ Gnathostomata"]
        P2["Positive: lung @ Sarcopterygii"]
        B1 -.->|blocks| ALL["Single sub-clade similarity<br/>summaries: Gnathostomata + Sarcopterygii + neg@Bilateria"]
        P1 --> ALL
        P2 --> ALL
    end

    subgraph disjoint["Disjoint descendants → TWO similarities"]
        B2["Negative: eye @ Bilateria"]
        PV["Positive: eye @ Vertebrata"]
        PA["Positive: eye @ Arthropoda"]
        B2 -.->|blocks| S1["Similarity 1<br/>eye, Vertebrata subtree"]
        B2 -.->|blocks| S2["Similarity 2<br/>eye, Arthropoda subtree"]
        PV --> S1
        PA --> S2
    end
```

### ⑦ Block-and-drop (no replacement)

If a group is blocked but **no** positive annotation exists for the same UBERON ID
set at any strict descendant of *R*, the term is **omitted entirely** from the result.
A negative alone does not define a usable comparison unit — curators must provide
sub-clade positives for the term to reappear in output.

---

# The three outcome paths (summary)

| Path | Condition | Result for blocked UBERON set *G* |
|------|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| **Fast path** | No negative for *G* at *R* or ancestors | Baseline similarity for *G* is kept |
| **Block-and-drop** | Negative exists; no positive for *G* at strict descendants | *G* absent from output |
| **Block-and-split** | Negative exists; positives for *G* at ≥1 strict descendant | One or more sub-clade similarities for *G* |

---

# Worked examples

The examples below use simplified taxon names. NCBI taxon IDs are shown where they
match the unit-test fixture in `AnatEntitySimilarityServiceTest`.

## Example A — Fast path (no negative)

**Query:** Actinopterygii (`7898`)

**Annotations (positive only relevant here):**

| Term | Taxon | Polarity |
|------|-------|----------|
| mouth | Eumetazoa | + |
| anus | Bilateria | + |
| swim bladder | Actinopterygii | + |
| lung | Gnathostomata | + (inherited) |

**No** negative annotation applies to Actinopterygii or its ancestors for these terms.

**Outcome:** Identical to `loadPositiveAnatEntitySimilarities` — four similarities
(mouth, anus, swim bladder, lung-with-ancestor-support).

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart LR
    Q["Query: Actinopterygii"] --> B["Baseline"]
    B --> R["Return baseline<br/>(no changes)"]
```

---

## Example B — Block-and-drop

**Query:** Cnidaria (`6073`)

**Annotations:**

| Term | Taxon | Polarity |
|------|-------|----------|
| mouth | Eumetazoa | + |
| mouth | Cnidaria | **−** (NOT homologous at this level) |

Cnidaria is a **leaf** in the test taxonomy (no strict descendants).

**Outcome:**

1. Baseline would include `mouth` (positive at Eumetazoa).
2. Negative at Cnidaria **blocks** `{mouth}`.
3. No descendant positive exists to substitute.
4. **Result:** empty set for `mouth`; no comparison group for mouth at Cnidaria.

This models the case "we know the Eumetazoa-level mouth annotation does not apply as
a single homology class within Cnidaria, and curators have not (yet) defined finer
sub-clade positives."

---

## Example C — Block-and-split (single sub-clade)

**Query:** Bilateria (`33213`)

**Annotations:**

| Term | Taxon | Polarity |
|------|-------|----------|
| swim bladder | Bilateria | **−** |
| swim bladder | Actinopterygii | + |
| mouth | Eumetazoa | + |
| anus | Bilateria | + |

**Outcome:**

| Term | Path | Result |
|------|------|--------|
| mouth | Fast (unblocked) | Kept from baseline |
| anus | Fast (unblocked) | Kept from baseline |
| swim bladder | Block-and-split | Baseline entry removed; **new** sub-clade similarity with summaries: positive @ Actinopterygii, negative @ Bilateria |

Expression data for swim bladder in ray-finned fishes can still be compared
multi-species **within the Actinopterygii homology class**, but data from other
bilaterian lineages that also use the label "swim bladder" (or related structures)
will **not** be pooled under a single Bilateria-wide group.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
flowchart TB
    SB["UBERON: swim bladder"]
    N["NOT homologous @ Bilateria"]
    P["Homologous @ Actinopterygii"]
    SIM["AnatEntitySimilarity<br/>requestedTaxon = Bilateria<br/>summaries: +Actinopterygii, −Bilateria"]

    SB --> N
    SB --> P
    N --> SIM
    P --> SIM
```

---

## Example D — Block-and-split (nested descendants merged)

**Query:** Bilateria (`33213`)

**Annotations:**

| Term | Taxon | Polarity |
|------|-------|----------|
| lung | Bilateria | **−** |
| lung | Gnathostomata | + |
| lung | Sarcopterygii | + |

Sarcopterygii is a **strict descendant** of Gnathostomata.

**Maximal taxon** among `{Gnathostomata, Sarcopterygii}` = **Gnathostomata**.

**Outcome:** One sub-clade similarity for `{lung}` with summaries:

- positive @ Gnathostomata
- positive @ Sarcopterygii (nested, merged into same group)
- negative @ Bilateria (documentation)

Not two separate lung similarities — nested positives collapse to the highest
(maximal) sub-clade root.

---

## Example E — Block-and-split (disjoint sub-clades) — conceptual

**Query:** Bilateria

**Annotations (typical eye case):**

| Term | Taxon | Polarity |
|------|-------|----------|
| eye (`UBERON:0000970`) | Bilateria | **−** |
| eye | Vertebrata | + |
| eye | Arthropoda | + |

Vertebrata and Arthropoda are **not** nested — both are maximal.

**Outcome:** **Two** `AnatEntitySimilarity` objects, both using the same
`AnatEntity` for `UBERON:0000970`, but:

| Similarity | Positive summaries | Species pooled |
|------------|-------------------|----------------|
| Eye / vertebrate clade | Vertebrata + neg @ Bilateria | Species under Vertebrata with eye data |
| Eye / arthropod clade | Arthropoda + neg @ Bilateria | Species under Arthropoda with eye data |

Human camera-eye expression is never grouped with fly compound-eye expression under
one "eye @ Bilateria" similarity.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
flowchart TB
    EYE["AnatEntity: eye<br/>(UBERON:0000970)"]
    NEG["Negative @ Bilateria"]
    V["Positive @ Vertebrata"]
    A["Positive @ Arthropoda"]

    EYE --> SIM1["AnatEntitySimilarity #1<br/>(vertebrate eye clade)"]
    EYE --> SIM2["AnatEntitySimilarity #2<br/>(arthropod eye clade)"]
    NEG --> SIM1
    NEG --> SIM2
    V --> SIM1
    A --> SIM2
```

---

## Example F — Multi-entity homology (positive baseline logic)

**Query:** Gnathostomata (`7776`), trusted annotations only

**Annotations:**

| Terms | Taxon | Polarity |
|-------|-------|----------|
| lung, swim bladder | Gnathostomata | + (multi-entity) |
| lung | Gnathostomata | + (single) |
| swim bladder | Actinopterygii | + (single) |

Because lung exists in sarcopterygians and swim bladder in actinopterygians (different
sub-clades), the **multi-entity** annotation `lung–swim bladder` is kept and the
corresponding single-entity annotations are suppressed.

**Negative annotations** on `{lung, swim bladder}` would block the **entire**
multi-entity set — not `{lung}` or `{swim bladder}` alone — unless matching
negatives exist for those exact sets separately.

---

# Downstream use in expression calls

`MultiSpeciesCallService.loadSimilarityExpressionCalls2` loads similarities via
`loadAnatEntitySimilaritiesRespectingNegations`, then groups per-species
`ExpressionCall2` records by `MultiSpeciesCondition` (anatomical + cell-type
similarity pairs).

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
flowchart LR
    GENES["Gene filters<br/>(one species each)"] --> LCA["LCA taxon R"]
    LCA --> RES["loadAnatEntitySimilarities<br/>RespectingNegations(R)"]
    RES --> SIMS["Set of AnatEntitySimilarity"]
    SIMS --> LOAD["Load ExpressionCall2<br/>per species"]
    LOAD --> GROUP["Group by MultiSpeciesCondition"]
    GROUP --> OUT["SimilarityExpressionCall2 stream"]

    style RES fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
    style OUT fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
```

**Practical consequence:** if eye is split into vertebrate and arthropod similarities,
a query spanning human and fruit fly returns **separate** expression call rows for
each homology class — never a single row that incorrectly merges both.

Each row's `multiSpeciesCondition.anatEntityTaxonScope` is the **least common ancestor**
of the species whose expression calls appear in that row. For a single species, that is the
species taxon itself (e.g. *Homo sapiens* for a human-only row); for several species, it is
the shared LCA taxon node from `TaxonService.loadLeastCommonAncestor` (e.g. Euarchontoglires
for human + mouse). This lets the frontend distinguish split homology groups that share the
same UBERON term but differ in species coverage.

---

# Limitations and non-goals

The current implementation **does not**:

1. **Infer sub-clades from negatives alone.** A negative without descendant positives
   drops the term (block-and-drop).
2. **Match partial UBERON sets.** A negative on `{A, B}` does not block or split
   `{A}` alone.
3. **Re-run multi-entity selection on descendant positives.** Sub-clade similarities
   are built directly from descendant summary annotations grouped by maximal taxon;
   the full `getValidMultipleEntityAnnotations` pipeline applies only to the baseline.
4. **Shadow negatives with intermediate positives.** A negative at Eumetazoa is not
   automatically cancelled by a positive at Bilateria when querying Gnathostomata;
   the blocked set remains blocked unless future curation rules add that logic.

Raw evidence lines (`RawSimilarityAnnotationDAO`) are not yet attached to
`AnatEntitySimilarityTaxonSummary` (noted as TODO on the model class).

# Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Summary annotation** | Curated rollup of raw evidence; stored with `negated` flag |
| **Blocked group** | UBERON ID set with a negative annotation at *R* or an ancestor |
| **Strict descendant** | Taxon below *R* in the NCBI hierarchy (not *R* itself) |
| **Maximal annotation taxon** | Among a set of annotation taxa, one that is not a descendant of any other in the set |
| **Sub-clade similarity** | `AnatEntitySimilarity` emitted by the slow path after block-and-split |
| **Baseline** | Output of positive-only logic before negative filtering |
